title: Gaussian comparison for normalized sums
statement: There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent real random variables on it, each satisfying the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: finite fourth absolute moment, mean zero, second moment one, third moment zero, and fourth moment at most $9$. For any $c\ge 0$ and any $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the difference between the expectation of $\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i)$ and its expectation under the standard Gaussian measure has absolute value at most $Kc n^{-1/4}$.
hypotheses_covered: Each $X_i$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions
replaced: There is a universal $K>0$ such that, for every $n>0$, probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, and independent real random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ with finite fourth moments, $\mathbb E X_i=\mathbb E X_i^3=0$, $\mathbb E X_i^2=1$, and $\mathbb E X_i^4\le9$, every $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $c\ge0$ satisfies $|\mathbb E\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_iX_i)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)|\le Kc\,n^{-1/4}$, where $Z$ is standard Gaussian.
